No new examination or patient interview is represented by this chart review.

1. Strongly suspected porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT), not yet biochemically confirmed, unifies the skin and hepatic/iron findings. Urgent care documented three months of recurrent tense bullae and slow-healing erosions on sun-exposed dorsal hands/fingers, fragility after minor trauma, milia and atrophic scars, facial hypertrichosis and reddish-brown morning urine with negative urine blood/protein. This is far more characteristic of PCT (hepatic UROD inhibition with porphyrin accumulation) than bullous pemphigoid. Iron, alcohol and smoking are important susceptibility factors. Pseudoporphyria and other cutaneous porphyrias remain alternatives if biochemical pattern is not typical; autoimmune bullous disease is not established.
